_meta.title: Neoclassical combining forms
_meta.description: Greek and Latin combining forms, shared across languages rather than belonging to any one of them. hypo + therm yields English hypothermic, Spanish hipotermia and French hypothermie from the same two morphemes. That is why this file sits in shared/ and not under en/: a learner who owns these morphemes owns vocabulary in every language that borrowed them, which is the cognate bridge first-language instruction depends on.
_meta.status: seed++ - broad Greek/Latin academic coverage. Large assistant-drafted batches (2026-07-22) are UNREVIEWED for origin/position/gloss; sound as inventory, not yet safe to teach from unchecked.
_meta._short_form_caveat: Forms of one or two letters (in, di, bi, an, tri, eu, con, sta, cip, fin) match the start of many unrelated words. A consumer must not split on them unless the REMAINDER is itself a listed morpheme or word - the same corner-is-not-corn-plus-er guard the base-morpheme inventory uses. Position alone is not enough here.
_meta._homographs_note: A form may appear more than once when one spelling is genuinely two morphemes (non=not vs non=nine). Such entries carry a `homograph` field. The list is keyed by (form, sense), not form alone, so a lookup returns EVERY sense and the remainder chooses - as a reader does.
_meta._reviewed_field: Every form carries `reviewed`. false = drafted by an AI assistant on 2026-07-22 from general knowledge; origin, position and gloss are plausible but unchecked and known to contain errors (false friends caught in flow: precipitate, pediatrician, non, nom). Sound as INVENTORY; not to be TAUGHT from until a maintainer or linguist flips the flag. Filter reviewed=true for student-facing use.

_provenance._note:
Who added what, when, and how. Recorded per BATCH rather than per entry: the data was created in batches, so batch records are honest and stay readable, while an entry needing individual sourcing (a teacher contribution, a single corrected form) may carry its own `prov` field.

Batches are identified by DATE and COMMIT SUBJECT, deliberately not by commit hash. A hash means nothing to a human auditor and breaks the moment history is ever rewritten; a subject line is stable, readable, and findable with `git log --grep`.

`method` is the load-bearing field. `authored` = compiled from facts by a person. `mined` = derived by code from a corpus named in PROVENANCE.md. `assistant` = drafted by an AI assistant at the maintainer's direction and accepted by the maintainer. All three produce uncopyrightable facts, so none affects the free-forever promise; recording which is which lets a downstream user filter and keeps the chain auditable by someone who was not here.

batches.scope: +5 Greek combining forms of cell biology (plast, derm, lys, troph…). Prompted by 'chloroplast' failing to segment while 'chlorophyll' succeeded — chloro was known, plast was not.

+1 combining form: thylak- from Greek thylakos (θύλακος) 'sac, pouch'. With -oid ('resembling') already listed, thylakoid now segments as thylak + oid = 'sac-like' — which is what a thylakoid is: a flattened disc-shaped sac stacked inside the chloroplast. Etymology supplied by Jason.

+10 forms. Chemical names are SYSTEMATIC morphology and readable as such: carbon dioxide = di- (two, already listed) + oxide (oxygen compound); the -ide/-ate/-ite series marks how much oxygen a salt carries. Roots (sulf, nitr, chlor, carbon, hydr) are included because the tiler needs one part of root length to accept a segmentation, so 'sulfate' tiles while a bare short-form pile-up does not. Origin 'chem' marks the coined nomenclature suffixes rather than claiming a false Greek etymology for them. Also mon- : mono- elides its final o before a vowel (monoxide, monarch), and without the elided form 'monoxide' could not segment.

batches.commit_subject: data: membr- / -ane, so membrane carries its meaning
batches.scope: +2 forms. membrane = membr + ane — Latin membrum 'limb, member' gives membrana, 'the skin covering one', the same root as member and dismember. The -ane entry names the Latin ending and explicitly warns it is NOT the chemistry -ane of methane: same spelling, different morpheme, and teaching them as one would be false.

_note: Neoclassical combining forms, from Greek and Latin. They belong in neither existing list: not `bases`, because they are not free words (there is no word 'therm'), and not `prefixes`, because prefixes attach to a free base while these combine with EACH OTHER - hypo+therm+ic has no free word anywhere in it. This is the layer that connects concepts rather than parses sentences: hypothermic and hyperthermic share `therm` and contrast only on hypo/hyper, and a learner who owns those three morphemes owns both words plus thermometer, thermal and isotherm.
_position: Position is not free. An initial form precedes a final one, and most are fixed to one slot: photo- and hypo- are initial, -logy and -meter final, while therm and graph occur in both. Recorded per entry rather than assumed, because a parser that tries every form in every slot will split words that should stay whole.

_self_example: The term for this category is itself one: neo-classic-al. `neo` is an initial combining form, `-ic` and `-al` are Class I suffixes stacking inside any Class II suffix that follows. A learner who owns neo, classic, -ic and -al owns the word that names the phenomenon.
_identity: A form is NOT an identity. `terr` is two unrelated Latin roots — terra (earth) and terrere (to frighten) — and a list keyed by spelling can hold only one of them, which is why `terrific` decomposed as earth-making. Entries that need distinguishing therefore carry an `id`; the rest are identified by `form`, so nothing else had to change. Read the id as `form.sense`.
_relations_note: Facts about how forms relate, previously written as English inside `note` fields where nothing could traverse or check them. The `note` text stays — it reads better than an edge — but the fact is now also machine-readable. Types: `variantOf` (one root, two shapes: scrib/script), `homographOf` (one spelling, unrelated roots: terr), `falseFriend` (confusably similar, unrelated: radi/radic), `translationOf` (same meaning, other classical language: terr/geo), `relatedTo` (a shared ancestor short of variance: luc/lum). Edges are undirected unless a type says otherwise, and BOTH endpoints must resolve to an id or a form in this file.
